observations: Photo 0 shows a dusty car alternator from the side with copper windings visible through cooling slots and a mounting foot at the bottom.
Photo 1 shows the pulley end of the alternator with mounting ears on both sides.
Photo 2 shows the rear shaft end of the alternator.
No brand name, model number, or part number is legible on the unit in any photo.
A watermark reading 'U-ZION LINKS AUTO'S' appears across all three photos.

claims.evidence: No document or photo shows country of origin.
Photos show only the exterior; no test or output reading is shown.
Photos cannot reveal internal bearing or noise condition.
Alternators have no odometer; photos cannot show usage history.
External photos cannot prove the unit was never disassembled.

risks.risk: Internal electrical or bearing failure not visible externally.
risks.proof: Video of the alternator spinning on a bench with voltage output reading.

risks.risk: Wrong fitment for buyer's vehicle due to unknown brand/model.
risks.proof: Clear photo of any label, plate, or part number on the housing.
risks.if_unproven: as a generic alternator with uncertain compatibility

risks.risk: Claimed Belgian origin and low mileage are false.
risks.proof: Import documents or seller video showing removal from a specific vehicle.

proof_requests: A clear photo of any label, plate, or stamping on the alternator body.
A video of the alternator being bench-tested showing charge output.
Seller documentation or video supporting the Belgium import claim.
response.reason: The item is visibly a car alternator and can be priced at its worst case as a non-working used unit; no missing shot prevents identifying what it is.
